column1: # Shared .env fixture: how scripts/collect-diagnostics.sh (load_env, awk) and scripts/collect-diagnostics.ps1 (Read-EnvSecrets) must read a .env.
# Both tests feed every case through the real script (sh: --scrub-stdin --env-file; ps1: -ScrubFile with -EnvFile): one line "keep <secret> keep"
# per secret must come out as "keep [hidden] keep" (the word "keep" proves that text next to a secret survives).
# Columns, separated by ONE TAB: name, the .env text, the secret values that must be hidden (joined by "|", no escapes in this column).
# Escapes in the .env text, decoded in ONE left-to-right pass: \n is a line feed, \r a carriage return, \t a tab, \\ one backslash.
# The rules (see load_env): only variables whose name holds PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN or KEY; blank and # lines are skipped, "export " is optional,
# the value starts after the first "=" (leading blanks dropped). A double-quoted value ends at the first unescaped quote, and BOTH its raw text and
# the text with \" and \\ unescaped are hidden; a single-quoted value ends at the first quote; an unquoted value ends at the first blank-then-# (space or
# tab) and loses trailing blanks. A value is taken as written: a $VAR in it is NOT expanded (compose would expand it). Values of under 4 characters are ignored;
# the part after the first ":" of a value is hidden too.
